articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Lays down uniform rules for transparency and disclosure, authorisation and supervision of CASPs, and issuance of asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens.

articles.title: Scope
articles.requirement: Applies to persons engaged in issuance, offer to the public, and admission to trading of crypto-assets, and to CASPs in the Union.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines crypto-asset, asset-referenced token, e-money token, CASP, distributed ledger technology, crypto-asset service, and other key terms.

articles.title: Exclusions
articles.requirement: Excludes crypto-assets qualifying as financial instruments, deposits, securitisation positions, insurance products, or pension products under existing EU law.

articles.title: Offers to the public of crypto-assets other than ARTs or EMTs
articles.requirement: No person shall make an offer to the public of crypto-assets unless a crypto-asset white paper has been drafted, notified to the competent authority, and published.

articles.title: Content of the crypto-asset white paper
articles.requirement: White paper must contain information about the issuer, project, rights and obligations, underlying technology, risks, and must be fair, clear, and not misleading.

articles.title: Marketing communications
articles.requirement: Marketing communications relating to an offer to the public must be clearly identifiable, fair, clear, not misleading, and consistent with the crypto-asset white paper.

articles.title: Notification of white paper
articles.requirement: White paper and marketing communications must be notified to the competent authority of the home Member State before publication.

articles.title: Publication of white paper
articles.requirement: The crypto-asset white paper must be published on the issuer's website and remain available for as long as the crypto-asset is held by the public.

articles.title: Right of withdrawal
articles.requirement: Consumers have a right of withdrawal within 14 calendar days of their agreement to purchase crypto-assets directly from the issuer, without incurring any cost.

articles.title: Authorisation to offer ARTs to the public
articles.requirement: No person shall offer asset-referenced tokens to the public or seek admission to trading unless authorised by the competent authority of the home Member State and approved white paper.

articles.title: Application for authorisation — ARTs
articles.requirement: Application must include programme of operations, governance arrangements, reserve of assets details, custody arrangements, complaint handling, and wind-down plan.

articles.title: Obligations of issuers of ARTs
articles.requirement: Issuers must act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interest of holders, maintain a reserve of assets, and have effective governance arrangements including risk management.

articles.title: Governance arrangements for ART issuers
articles.requirement: ART issuers must have robust governance including clear organisational structure, well-defined lines of responsibility, effective risk management, adequate internal control mechanisms, and fit and proper management.

articles.title: Own funds requirements for ART issuers
articles.requirement: ART issuers must maintain own funds equal to the higher of €350,000 or 2% of the average amount of the reserve assets, or a quarter of fixed overheads of the preceding year.

articles.title: Reserve of assets — composition and management
articles.requirement: ART issuers must constitute and maintain a reserve of assets backing the token, invested in secure, low-risk assets, segregated from the issuer's own assets, and held by qualified custodians.

articles.title: Custody of reserve assets
articles.requirement: Reserve assets must be held in custody by credit institutions or authorised crypto-asset custodians, ensuring segregation and availability for timely redemption.

articles.title: Prohibition of interest on ARTs
articles.requirement: Issuers of ARTs and CASPs shall not grant interest or any other benefit related to the length of time during which a holder holds asset-referenced tokens.

articles.title: Significant ARTs
articles.requirement: EBA shall classify ARTs as significant based on criteria including customer base size, value of issued tokens, number/value of transactions, cross-border activity, and interconnectedness.

articles.title: Authorisation as credit institution for EMTs
articles.requirement: Only credit institutions or electronic money institutions authorised under Directive 2009/110/EC may issue e-money tokens within the Union.

articles.title: Issuance and redeemability of EMTs
articles.requirement: EMT issuers must issue e-money tokens at par value on receipt of funds and redeem at par value at any time at the request of the holder, free of charge.

articles.title: Prohibition of interest on EMTs
articles.requirement: Issuers of EMTs and CASPs shall not grant interest or any other benefit related to the length of time during which a holder holds e-money tokens.

articles.title: EMT white paper
articles.requirement: Issuers of EMTs must draw up and publish a white paper containing the information specified in Annex III before offering EMTs to the public.

articles.title: Significant EMTs
articles.requirement: EBA shall classify EMTs as significant based on the same criteria as significant ARTs. Significant EMT issuers are subject to additional requirements.

articles.title: Conditions for CASP authorisation
articles.requirement: Only legal persons with a registered office in a Member State may apply for CASP authorisation. CASPs must meet fit and proper, governance, prudential, and operational requirements.

articles.title: Application for authorisation as CASP
articles.requirement: Application must include programme of operations, proof of own funds, governance arrangements, internal control mechanisms, ICT security policies, business continuity, and complaint handling procedures.

articles.title: Assessment of application and granting of authorisation
articles.requirement: Competent authority must assess completeness within 25 working days and decide on authorisation within 40 working days, verifying all regulatory requirements are met.

articles.title: Notification of changes and renewal
articles.requirement: CASPs must notify competent authorities of any material change to conditions of initial authorisation at least 30 calendar days before the intended change.

articles.title: Obligation to act honestly, fairly, and professionally
articles.requirement: CASPs must act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interests of their clients and provide fair, clear, and not misleading information.

articles.title: Prudential requirements for CASPs
articles.requirement: CASPs must have own funds at least equal to the higher of the permanent minimum capital requirement or a quarter of fixed overheads of the preceding year.

articles.title: Custody and administration of crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs providing custody must establish a custody policy, segregate client assets, ensure clients' assets are not used for own account, and return crypto-assets without undue delay.

articles.title: Exchange of crypto-assets for funds or other crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs providing exchange services must establish a non-discriminatory commercial policy, publish firm prices or methodology for determining prices, and execute orders at quoted prices.

articles.title: Portfolio management of crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs providing portfolio management must assess suitability, act in the client's best interest, and provide periodic statements of activities and performance.

articles.title: Prohibition of insider dealing
articles.requirement: No person in possession of inside information relating to crypto-assets shall use that information to acquire or dispose of crypto-assets, or recommend or induce another person to do so.

articles.title: Prohibition of market manipulation
articles.requirement: No person shall engage in market manipulation including wash trading, spoofing, dissemination of false or misleading information, or any other artifice to secure the price of crypto-assets at an abnormal level.
